Master list of drawings is  available and is partially updated. Control copy drawings are not available for all parts. I.e the control copy drawing for A601 HL HCM HT SINK HSG 4755-69-00-00 is not evident.
Critical parameters are not defined in the control plan.
Process sheets, WI, and inspection & test instructions are available however, their interlinkage with the control plan is not evident.
In-process inspection and set-up approval reports are partially available. I.e SPM drilling and tapping inspection reports are not available.
Packaging instructions are available at the final inspection stage with limited information. Detailed packaging standard needs to be made available at the final inspection stage.
Operators are not aware of the drawing SC/CC parameters.
Operator is aware of the JH activities; however, the JH checklist is only partially filled out as per the inspection frequency.
Awareness of customer complaints among operators and inspectors is evident; however, quality alerts are not available at the relevant stages.
After a customer complaint, all related documents are partially reviewed and updated.

Manufacturing Process Audit Plan (Doc No.: SI-PRD-F-06) is available for all manufacturing processes; however, shot blasting, vibro, lancing, conventional machining, and buffing processes are excluded. Manufacturing Process Report (Doc No.: SI-PRD-F-07) needs to be reviewed and updated for in-process inspection, tool life monitoring, and PM activities.

In-house rejection monitoring and action plans are in place as per the 80:20 Pareto matrix. However, supplier defect rejections are not being monitored, and corresponding action plans are not evident. For example, casting defects such as short fill, blow holes, and carbon marks are the top contributors, but corresponding action plans are not evident.
Action plan is not available for the top five defect phenomena.
Poka yoke are not incorporate into the control plan.
Master list of master/limit samples is available; however, the defined validation frequency is not adhered to.
Process validation reports are not available

PM plan is available for all machines and utility equipment (Doc No.: SI-MAINT-F-01). However, a PM plan is required for all machines, and PM should be conducted accordingly. Currently, for the conventional drilling machine, a combined PM plan and reports are available.

Breakdown history is available along with breakdown causes and corrective actions (Document No.: SI-MAINT-F-07). However, the analysis needs to be structured in a more systematic manner to clearly identify the root cause and corresponding countermeasures.
Monthly preventive checkpoints are verified as per the defined frequency, and the CBM methodology is being followed. However, MTTR and MTBF targets are not defined and are not being monitored.
Product Layout Inspection plan is available ( Doc no-SI-PRD-F-22) and as per planner records are partially available.

Partial compliance with the calibration plan is evident. Total of 206 equipment are available; however, 9 equipment have been overdue since January 2026. Additionally, calibration acceptance criteria are not clearly specified.

MSA instrument family-wise MSA plan (Doc No.: SI-QAD-F-15) is available however, partial compliance is evident. I.e, the micrometer 75–100 mm study was planned for March 2026, but the actual study was not performed.

Quality Engineer is aware of the MSA study and its criteria. However, the MSA Study WI is not available, and acceptance criteria are not specified in the study report. Attribute study is not effectively performed, as only two appraisers were evaluated using OK samples, and no NG samples were included.
